description: This "figure" is not a scientific figure: the supplied image is a publisher's CrossMark "Check for updates" badge, a square raster icon with a light grey gradient background. It consists of a red, ribbon/bookmark-shaped pentagon (rectangular top with a notched V bottom edge) centred inside a thick circular ring that is split into two arcs — a blue arc occupying roughly the upper-right half and a yellow arc occupying the lower-left half. Beneath the ring, two lines of black sans-serif text read "Check for" on the first line and "updates" on the second, both centred. No axes, no scale bar, no legend, no data points, no micrograph, no sample label and no numeric value appear anywhere in the image. It therefore carries no materials-science data and cannot be linked to any panel of the parent paper (Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel, grain size 8.7-32 μm, solution treatment 950-1150 ℃). It was almost certainly captured from the article PDF as a stray embedded graphic rather than being a numbered Figure. Nothing can be interpreted from it about oxide film formation or corrosion behaviour.

subfigures.description: CrossMark 'Check for updates' publisher badge: a red bookmark/ribbon symbol inside a circular ring split into a blue upper-right arc and a yellow lower-left arc, with the two-line caption text 'Check for updates' below it, on a light grey gradient background.

observations.observation: The image shows the CrossMark 'Check for updates' badge: a red bookmark-shaped symbol inside a ring composed of a blue arc and a yellow arc.
The text 'Check for updates' is printed in black sans-serif type in two centred lines directly beneath the circular symbol.
The badge sits on a plain light grey gradient background with no frame, axes, gridlines, scale bar or legend.
No data, curves, micrograph, spectrum, map, table or schematic content is present; the image conveys no materials-science information.
No sample label, composition, processing condition or numeric value is printed anywhere in the image.
No caption was extracted for this figure, so no caption-based claim can be attached to it.

The parent paper concerns Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels with grain sizes of 8.7-32 μm produced by solution treatment between 950 ℃ and 1150 ℃, but this image contains nothing that relates to those samples.
